sentences.text: Leptoceratops is a genus of ceratopsian dinosaur now placed in its own family, Leptoceratopsidae.
This animal was approximately 2 meters long, though a reconstructed complete skeleton measures about 1.81 meters.
It featured a large head with a strong jaw, minimal frill, and an increased number of vertebrae before the pelvis.
Barnum Brown named the genus in 1914 after the first discovery in Alberta in 1910.
The type species, Leptoceratops gracilis, was defined based on remains from the Scollard Formation.
Charles M. Sternberg uncovered additional skeletons in that same formation in 1947.
Unique teeth showed wear patterns driven by a mammal-like jaw rotation while chewing various plants.
A large ridge above the maxillary teeth suggests it had a muscled cheek pouch to assist in shredding vegetation.
It is possible that this dinosaur dug and lived in multi-generational burrows.
Leptoceratops lived during the Late Cretaceous period, specifically the Maastrichtian age, between 65.5 and 66.1 million years ago.
Specimens were found in the middle Hell Creek Formation and a semi-humid floodplain environment with braided streams.

Comparisons later showed that a Montana specimen should be placed in its own genus, Montanoceratops. The assignment of a Wyoming specimen was questioned due to similarities with Prenoceratops and potential misidentification. Phylogenetic analyses have resulted in unresolved relationships within the strict consensus of Leptoceratopsidae, partly because new taxa like Ferrisaurus and Gremlin contribute to a lack of resolution due to fragmentary fossil evidence.
